verdict: PR #15312 closed the high defect: the schedule now stays fixed to the award, so a late filing no longer moves later deadlines (checked: 2027-01-15, -5 days, Overdue). It also fixed the impossible-date roll-over, the false 'smallest award' sentence and the README event list, and pinned both status boundaries in tests. It left the medium spec gap open, writing it down as a known gap instead: on arrival a federal quarterly award still read Overdue 14 days before its 30-day deadline, and an award past its period of performance showed a periodic report a year out instead of an overdue final report (2 CFR 200.329, 200.344). The explainer still taught 'award date plus interval' as the rule. Three of six seeded mutants survived. It does not meet the bar on arrival: correctness, claims and verification are 2. This PR adds optional reporting-lag, award-end and final-report fields with tests pinned to the eCFR dates, rewrites the explainer FAQ, and flags overspending. A later round should re-score it.
